Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 39605 of 2024

Applicant :- Smt. Sunita Rajput
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Anurag Shukla,Prabhat Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Sudarshan Singh, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Anurag Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State.
2.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 418 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 506, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Chakeri, District Kanpur Nagar during pendency of the trial.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, she has been made accused in the present matter along with her other family members including husband of the deceased.
4.

He further submits, however, during investigation informant and his family members supported the prosecution case but during trial when informant i.e. father of the deceased and his wife i.e.
mother of the deceased appeared before the trial court as PW-1 and PW-2 then they did not support the prosecution case and have been declared hostile.

He further submits, their statements recorded Smt. Sunita Rajput vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9593995/
1 by the trial court have been annexed along with affidavit and supplementary affidavit filed in support of instant bail application.

sentences.text:
5. He further submits, even from the post mortem, it reflects deceased died due to hanging,
therefore, prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death.

6. He further submits that applicant is a lady and there is no specific allegation against her and she is not having any criminal history and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 29.06.2024.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant including the fact that informant and mother of the deceased both have been declared hostile by the trial court.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. However, it reflects, daughter-in-law of the applicant died within two months of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there was also allegation of demand of dowry but applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and there was no specific allegation against her and post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging, therefore, this Court finds merit in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death.

10. Further, from the record it reflects that during trial when parents of the deceased including informant i.e. her father appeared before the trial court as PW-1 and PW-2 then they did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile.
11. Further, applicant is a lady and she is not having any criminal history and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 29.06.2024.

12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant - Smt. Sunita Rajput be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from Smt. Sunita Rajput vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9593995/
2 disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
15.

16. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
